en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of Fearlessness Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court-Dispersing Grandee, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
and Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, the Subject Faxian, by imperial decree.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"Listen attentively, for I shall now proclaim the Fearless Dhāraṇī.
This dhāraṇī is able to pacify and eliminate all calamities for sentient beings."
Bhikṣus, if there are those who hear and uphold this,
the merit they obtain will be immeasurable and boundless.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:

At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
Again, he addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"If a son or daughter of good family,
upon hearing this dhāraṇī, gives rise to a heart of sincere resolve..."
With reverent faith, they shall make offerings, read, recite, receive, and uphold it;
whether copying it with their own hands or having others copy it,
and explaining it extensively to others so that it may be widely propagated.
Such a person shall not be harmed by the perils of kings, the perils of water or fire,
the perils of weapons and warfare, or the perils of enemies and bandits;
furthermore, they shall not be harmed by the perils of yakṣas or the perils of imprisonment.
The perils of thunder and hail; the peril of lightning;
the peril of being swept away by the great ocean; the peril of being bitten by the venom of pythons;
the perils of lions, mad elephants, fierce tigers, and evil beasts; and the perils of famine and pestilence.
Thus, none of these calamities shall cause harm, and they shall all be liberated from even the most terrifying fears.
At that time, the assembly of bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
rejoiced, accepted it with faith, prostrated, and withdrew.
The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of Fearlessness Spoken by the Buddha.
